973:
(a) Reasonable fees sufficient to cover the cost of administration, inspection, publication of notice and similar matters may be charged to applicants for rezoning applications (amendments to the map or text), variance applications, conditional use applications, an appeal from action of the building official or the administrative official and other administrative relief. The amount of the fees charged shall be as set forth by the city.
(b) Fees established in accordance with subsection (a) of this section shall be paid upon submission of a signed application or notice of appeal.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 13-7)
976:
There shall be a planning commission consisting of five members.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 3-1)
977:
(a) Planning commission members shall be appointed by the mayor and city council. Members shall serve three-year staggered terms and may continue until their successors are duly appointed. The mayor and city council shall have the right to remove any member of the planning commission for cause.
(b) The planning commission shall annually elect one of its members as chairperson.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 3-1.1)
978:
(a) The planning commission shall establish a regular meeting schedule.
(b) Minutes shall be kept of all planning commission proceedings.
(c) All planning commission meetings shall be open to the public. Whenever feasible, the agenda for each meeting shall be made available in advance of the meeting.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 3-1.2)
979:
(a) A quorum for the planning commission shall consist of a majority of its membership (excluding vacant seats). A quorum is necessary for the planning commission to take official action.
(b) All actions of the planning commission shall be taken by a majority vote, a quorum being present.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 3-1.3)
980:
(a) Specific limitations of powers of the planning commission. The planning commission does not have the power to amend any zoning ordinance, to rezone any land, to declare this chapter or any amendment thereto invalid or to allow any use not permitted by this chapter.
(b) Duties of the planning commission.
(1) Recommend to the mayor and city council changes to this chapter that the planning commission believes are appropriate.
(2) Recommend to the mayor and city council approval, disapproval or other action on all requests for zoning changes as provided in this chapter.
(3) Dispense general information about this chapter to the public upon request.
(4) Questions involving interpretation of the zoning map ("official map"), including district boundary lines and lot lines, as provided in section 46-54.
(5) Questions involving final interpretation for all provisions of this chapter.
(6) Advise the mayor and city council on matters of zoning as it may deem appropriate.
(7) Conduct such other business and affairs as may be, from time to time, designated by the mayor and city council.
(8) Appeals. Appeals where it is alleged there is error in any order, requirement, decision or determination made by the building official or the administrative official in the enforcement of this chapter. Such appeals shall be made in accordance with the following:
a. Purpose; procedure. An appeal to the planning commission may be taken by any person, firm or corporation aggrieved by any decision of the building official or administrative official. Such appeal shall be made within 15 days following the notification of the decision appealed from, by filing with the city clerk a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof. The official from whom the appeal is taken shall forthwith transmit to the planning commission all the papers constituting the record upon which the action appealed from was taken.
b. Stay of proceedings. An appeal stays all legal proceeding in furtherance of the action appealed from, unless the official from whom the appeal is taken certifies to the planning commission, after the notice of appeal has been filed, that, by reason of facts stated in the certificate, a stay would, in his opinion, cause imminent peril to life and property. In such case, proceedings shall not be stayed otherwise than by a restraining order which may be granted by the planning commission or by a court of competent jurisdiction, on notice to the official or office from whom the appeal is taken, and on due cause shown.
c. Evidence. The appellant and any public agency or private individual shall be entitled to present evidence on matters before the planning commission. Evidence supporting the grant or denial of an appeal shall be submitted only through the administrative official or to the planning commission in a public meeting.
d. Withdrawal of appeal. Any appeal may be withdrawn upon written notice to the administrative official, but no appeal shall be withdrawn after the posting of a hearing notice as required in section 46-319(c), and prior to the planning commissions' action thereon without formal consent of the planning commission.
e. Decision. The planning commission may, in conformity with the terms of this chapter, reverse or affirm, in whole or in part, or may modify the order, requirement, decision or determination appealed from, and, to that end, shall have the powers of the building official or administrative official. The planning commission may direct the issuance of a permit. It shall be the duties of the administrative official to carry out the decisions of the planning commission.
(9) Conditional uses. Some zoning districts permit certain uses only upon approval of the planning commission. These uses are identified in this article as conditional uses and are not generally allowed in a particular zoning district, or in any other zoning districts, because the special characteristics of such uses create impacts on surrounding areas. Such uses may be allowed under special conditions. The granting of a conditional use does not constitute a permanent change in zoning or use. The conditional use may be forfeited if it does not meet the criteria provided in this section. Generally, a conditional use shall be compatible with the applicable zoning district under special conditions.
a. Conditional use approval. Conditional uses shall be permitted subject to an approval by the planning commission according to procedures established in section 46-319. The required review shall determine whether the uses conform to the standards set forth in subsection (b)(9)b of this section.
b. Conditional use standards. The conditional use shall be approved if it meets all the following factors:
1. A rezoning to a more intensive zoning district, which contains that use as a use by right, would not be appropriate for the property.
2. The location and character of the conditional use shall be compatible with the community development pattern and consistent with the needs of the neighborhood.
3. The conditional use will not be injurious to the use and enjoyment of the natural environment or of other property in the immediate vicinity, or diminish and impair property values within the surrounding neighborhood.
4. The conditional use will not increase state or local expenditures in relation to the cost of servicing or maintaining neighborhood properties.
c. Additional conditions and development standards. The planning commission may impose any additional conditions and development standards, along with the grant of the conditional use, as may be necessary to protect the health, safety and welfare of surrounding landowners, neighborhoods and workers.
(10) Variances. The planning commission shall hear and decide applications for variances from the development requirements of this article, but only in individual cases of practical difficulty or unnecessary hardship. This includes exceptional narrowness, shallowness or shape of a specific piece of property, which at the time of adoption of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived, was a lot or plat of record; or where, by reason of exceptional topographic conditions or other extraordinary or exceptional conditions of a piece of property, the strict application of the said development requirements of this chapter would result in practical difficulties to, or undue hardship upon, the owner of such property. However, the planning commission shall not be authorized to grant a density variance or a use variance to permit a use in a district in which the use is prohibited.
a. No variance shall be authorized unless the planning commission finds that all of the following conditions exist:
1. The special circumstances or conditions applying to the building or land in question are peculiar to such premises and do not apply generally to other land or buildings in the vicinity.
2. The granting of the application is necessary for the preservation and enjoyment of a property right and not merely to serve as a convenience to the applicant.
3. The condition from which relief of a variance is sought did not result from action by the applicant.
4. The authorization of the variance will not impair an adequate supply of light and air to adjacent property or unreasonably increase the congestion in public streets, increase the danger of fire, imperil the public safety, unreasonably diminish or impair established property values within the surrounding areas or in any other respect impair the health, safety, comfort, morals or general welfare of the inhabitants of the city.
b. In reviewing an application for a variance, the burden of showing that the variance should be granted shall be upon the person applying thereof. Additional provisions are as follows:
1. Approval of request; conditions. In granting a variance, the planning commission may attach thereto such conditions regarding the location, character and other features of the proposed building, structure or use as it may deem advisable so that the purpose of this chapter will be served and to provide adequately for the maintenance of the integrity and character of the zone in which such permit is granted.
2. Approval of request; guarantees. When necessary, the planning commission may require guarantees, in such form as it deems proper, to insure that conditions designated in connection therewith are being or will be complied with. Where any condition under which a request has been granted appears to have been violated, the planning commission may hold a public hearing thereon to determine whether or not the permit theretofore granted shall be terminated.
3. Grant of variance. The planning commission, when granting a variance, may establish a time period for said variance. The grant of a variance shall be stated in the minutes with the reasons for departure from the strict application of this chapter and the conditions under which the variance was granted. Any variance granted shall terminate automatically when the use ceases to be in full compliance with any conditions imposed by the planning commission, when the use has been abandoned or when the building permit shall have expired.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 3-1.4)
981:
(a) Scheduling. Within a reasonable time after receiving an application for an appeal, variance, or conditional use and before making a decision, the planning commission shall schedule a public hearing.
(b) Application.
(1) The application and fee as determined by the city for a hearing and decision on requests for an appeal (additionally, a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof, shall be filed with the city clerk within 15 days following the notification of the decision appealed from), variance, or conditional use shall be filed with the administrative official on forms provided by the city at least 30 days prior to the next scheduled planning commission meeting. Each application shall contain such information as the administrative official may require to enable the planning commission to make its decision.
(2) Additional requirements for a variance request. Each application for a variance shall include a plat drawn to scale showing the following information:
a. All property lines, with dimensions.
b. Location of buildings and other structures, creeks and easements referenced to the property line of the property in question.
c. The North Arrow, land district and land lot marker.
d. Location of setback lines or other dimensional requirements from which the variance is sought.
(c) Notice of hearing.
(1) Published in newspaper. The planning commission shall publish once in a newspaper of general circulation in the county a written notice of such public hearing at least 15 but not more than 45 days prior to the public hearing. The public notice shall indicate the time, place and nature of the appeal, variance or conditional use to be considered by the planning commission. Upon the hearing any party may appear in person, or by agent, or by attorney.
(2) Posted on public sign. Additionally, at least 15 days before the scheduled public hearing, the administrative official shall post, in a conspicuous place on the property, a sign at least two feet by three feet in size. It shall set forth the time, place and purpose of the public hearing before the planning commission. Acts of vandalism or natural occurrences limiting the effectiveness of notice by a sign posted on the property shall not invalidate any proceedings or action taken under this article.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 3-1.5)
982:
Any person severally or jointly aggrieved by any decision of the planning commission or with any official charged with the enforcement of any order, requirement or decision of said planning commission, may take within 30 days thereafter an appeal to the superior court of the county. The appellant shall furnish the planning commission a written notice of appeal specifying the judgement or decision from which the appeal is taken. In case of such appeal, the planning commission shall cause a transcript of the proceedings in the case to be certified to the court to which the appeal is taken. Upon failure to file said appeal within 30 days, the said decision of the planning commission shall be final.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 3-1.6)
985:
The mayor and city council may from time to time, amend these regulations set forth in this chapter or the boundaries of the zoning districts established on the zoning map subject to the following conditions:
(1) No amendment shall become effective unless it shall have been initiated by either the city council or the planning commission, the property owners, or an individual who has the owners' power of attorney authorizing him to act, or a request signed by 60 percent of the property owners who hold not less than 60 percent of the affected land.
(2) As used in this article, the term "amendment" means both a change to the official map and a change to the text of this chapter unless otherwise indicated. All applications for amendment must first be reviewed by the planning commission, who will then make a written recommendation to the mayor and city council. The power to approve and enact an amendment rests solely within the legislative discretion of the city council.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 14-1)
986:
(a) Application for amendment. All proposed amendments shall be initiated by an application with the city clerk on forms provided by the city. A standard fee shall be paid with the application in the amount of the advertising costs for the required public hearing. Application for amendment of these regulations may be in the form of a proposal for amendment of the text of regulations or a proposal for amendment of the zoning map. Applications for amendment shall be transmitted by the city clerk to the city council and shall include the following:
(1) All applications shall be signed by the applicant, and shall state the applicant's name and address.
(2) In case of a text amendment, the application shall set forth the new text to be added and the existing text to be amended.
(3) In the case of a map amendment, the application shall set forth the following:
a. The area in which the requested change is located, the land proposed to be reclassified and the location with respect to the nearby public roads in common use;
b. A suitable description showing the location, shape and dimensions of the property;
c. The present zoning classification for such land;
d. The area of the land proposed to be reclassified stated in square feet if less than one acre and in acres if one acre or more;
e. A survey prepared by a registered land surveyor which accurately depicts the property sought to be rezoned.
(b) Requirements met before sign posted. All of the requirements of subsection (a) of this section shall be met before the advertisement is published and signs are posted.
(c) Applicant cannot be in violation of this chapter. No application will be accepted from any person regarding any property that is in violation of this chapter. If the property, at the time of application, which is the subject of an amendment or any other action of the planning commission, is found to be in violation of this chapter, then the mayor and city council will not accept and/or process any application from that applicant until the applicant voluntarily removes or changes the cause of the violation or ceases to be in violation. The applicant must then notify the administrative official that he is no longer in violation and obtains a release from the administrative official as to the violation. Once released, the mayor and city council will then accept the application for amendment of this chapter.
(d) Erection of sign. Within three days after acceptance for filing an application for a map amendment, the applicant shall erect a sign, to be furnished by the administrative official, on the land to be rezoned.
(1) Such sign shall be erected by the applicant within ten feet of whatever boundary line of such land abuts the most traveled public road; if no public road abuts thereon, then such sign shall be erected to face in such manner as may be most readily seen by the public. The lower edge of the sign face shall be not less than 2½ feet above the ground. The sign, furnished by the administrative official, shall show the application number, the present zoning classification, the proposed zoning classification, the scheduled date, time and place of the public hearing, and the telephone number of city hall to call for further information.
(2) Any such sign shall be maintained at all times by the applicant until a decision on the application has been made public by the governing authority. The sign shall be returned to the administrative official within five days thereafter.
(e) Referral to planning commission. After acceptance of application for amendment, the mayor and city council shall transmit a copy thereof to the planning commission for its review and recommendation. It will study the proposed amendment and determine if it meets the standards as enumerated in section 46-346. The planning commission shall then submit its findings to the mayor and city council within 30 days from the date it received the petition. If the planning commission fails to submit a report within a 30-day period, it shall be deemed to have approved the requested changes of departure.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 14-2)
987:
(a) The exercise of the zoning power of the city shall constitute an effort to balance the interest of the community in promoting the public health, safety, morality and general welfare against the right of property owners to the unrestricted use of their property. Prior to the public hearing, the planning commission shall prepare a written assessment as part of its review and recommendation of the rezoning proposal using the following standards. These standards are determined to be relevant in balancing the interest in promoting the public health, safety, morality and general welfare against the right to the unrestricted use of the property.
(b) The following standards for assessment of a rezoning request shall govern the exercise of the zoning power pursuant to the authority and mandates of O.C.G.A. § 36-66-1 et seq.:
(1) Existing uses and zoning of nearby property.
(2) The extent to which property values are diminished by the existing zoning restrictions.
(3) The extent to which the destruction of property values of the applicant promotes the health, safety, morals or general welfare of the public.
(4) The relative gain to the public, as compared to the hardship imposed upon the individual property owner.
(5) The suitability of the subject property for the existing zoning classification.
(6) The length of time the property has been vacant as zoned considered in the context of land development in the area in the vicinity of the property.
(7) The possible creation of an isolated district unrelated to adjacent and nearby districts.
(8) The population density pattern and possible increase or overtaxing of the load on public facilities including, but not limited to, schools, utilities and streets.
(9) The cost of the local government in providing, improving, increasing or maintaining public utilities, schools, streets and public safety measure.
(10) Impact on the environment, including, but not limited to, drainage, soil erosion and sedimentation, flooding, air quality and water quality and quantity.
(11) Whether the proposed change will be a deterrent to the value or improvement of development of adjacent property in accordance with existing regulations.
(12) Whether there are substantial reasons why the property cannot be used in accordance with existing zoning.
(13) The aesthetic effect of existing and future use of the property as it relates to the surrounding area.
(14) Any other factors relevant to the balancing interest in promoting the public health, safety, morality or general welfare against a right to unrestricted use of property.
(c) The city shall consider any proposed amendment properly initiated in light of the factors set forth in subsection (b) of this section. In evaluating the factors set forth in subsection (b) of this section, it shall be the policy of the city to exercise its zoning power in conformity with the policy and intent of the city comprehensive plan insofar as that plan is current in its application to the specific property that is the subject of the proposed amendment. It is further the policy of the city to exercise the zoning power for purposes of assuring the compatibility of use of adjacent and nearby properties and the preservation of the economic value of adjacent and nearby properties while enabling a reasonable use of all property.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 14-3)
988:
Before taking action on a proposed amendment, the mayor and the city council shall hold a public hearing thereon. A public hearing shall be conducted at the time and place specified by the mayor and city council and as set forth in the public notice described in section 46-348. The purpose of such hearing shall be to present to the public the proposed zoning amendment, and to receive comments thereon from the public. The mayor and city council shall consider the proceedings and comments of such hearing on the proposed zoning amendment in making a final decision on whether to approve or deny the amendment application. The mayor and city council shall prescribe the rules of order for its deliberations on matters with which it is charged under this article, and said rules of order shall be consistent with the general requirements and purposes set forth in this article and other general laws of the state concerning conduct of proceedings of public commissions, bodies and governmental units.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 14-4)
989:
Public notice of the hearing on a proposed amendment to this chapter shall be given as hereinafter set forth:
(1) Notice published in newspaper. At least 15, but not more than 45 days prior to the date set by the mayor and city council for the hearing, a written notice shall be published in a newspaper of general circulation in the county setting forth the time, place, and purpose of the hearing. Such notice shall contain a summary of the proposed amendment, if a text amendment, and in the case of a map amendment, the location of the property, its area, name or owner, and the proposed change or classification. The cost of such newspaper notice shall be paid by the applicant for the zoning amendment.
(2) Notice to interested parties. A notice shall be sent to the applicant and the planning commission, by mail, of the date, time, and place of hearing. All application files shall be placed in the custody of the administrative official and shall be open to public inspection during the regular office hours.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 14-5)
990:
The following policies and procedures shall govern the conduct of public hearings under this article:
(1) The hearing shall be convened by the mayor at the time and place scheduled.
(2) The mayor shall open any hearing with an explanation of the purpose of the hearing and a description of the general rules for the conduct of the hearing. The mayor or his delegate may describe the authority and role of the city council in any zoning decision.
(3) The mayor shall review the procedures for holding the public hearing which shall be as follows:
a. No person may speak until recognized by the mayor. Upon rising to speak, the person recognized must first state his name and address.
b. The person speaking will be allowed two minutes to express opinions and make points on each separate element of the proposed zoning revisions which he wishes to address; provided, however, that no person shall speak longer than an aggregate of ten minutes.
c. Any remark amounting to attack on the character or personal integrity of another individual, or comment not factually supportable, or comment in the form of an emotional outburst, shall be non-germane to the purpose of any hearing and may be ruled out of order.
d. Additional persons will be recognized in accordance with the procedure set forth above for the purpose of addressing additional issues and making additional points, but no speaker shall be allowed to address points which have already been thoroughly discussed.
(4) In the case of each petition for amendment to this chapter, the mayor shall allow the applicant, or the agent for the applicant, to speak first and to present the arguments of the applicant in favor of the proposed amendment.
(5) After each person in attendance has been afforded an opportunity to speak, the mayor shall present to those in attendance the results of the evaluation prepared by the planning commission as required by section 46-346.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 14-6)
991:
(a) When the public hearing is conducted by the city council at a regular council meeting, action may be taken approving or rejecting the proposal at that meeting, or the council may table the question for consideration at its next regular meeting or a called meeting to be held no later than the next regular meeting.
(b) The planning commission's role in any zoning decision shall be advisory only. Any zoning decision shall be made by the mayor and city council who shall either approve or disapprove the proposed zoning amendment.
(c) Public notice of decision. No later than the day after a decision on the question has been reached, the results of such action shall be posted as a regular public notice at the place for such notices in the city hall.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 14-7)
992:
Appeals from the decision of the mayor and city council regarding the adoption or disapproval of a zoning amendment shall be made in accordance with the judicial review provided in section 46-380.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 14-8)
993:
If the city council shall take official action defeating a proposed zoning amendment which seeks to rezone property, the same property may not be considered again for rezoning until the expiration of 12 months from the date of the official action of the city council. However, on receipt of written documentation by the original party requesting the zoning change that conditions have changed substantially within the city or area sufficient to justify the reconsideration of a zoning change and an earlier review of the proposed change, the mayor and city council may waive the mandatory delay period and authorize the reconsideration of the proposed change as though it were a newly requested zoning change. In such instances, the request for a zoning change shall comply fully with the requirements of this article.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 14-9)
996:
Any person found in violation of any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction, shall be punished according to the law. Each offense shall constitute a separate offense for each day such violation continues.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 13-8)
997:
If any building is erected, constructed, reconstructed, altered, repaired, converted or maintained, or any building or land is used in violation of this chapter, the administrative official or any other appropriate authority or any adjacent or neighboring property owner who would be damaged by such violation, in addition to other remedies, may institute injunction, mandamus or other appropriate action in proceeding to prevent such violation. In the event that the owner of a manufactured home does not meet the requirements of this chapter, then water and sewage hook-ups will not be connected.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 13-9)
998:
Any person severally or jointly aggrieved by any decision of the city council or with any official charged with the enforcement of any order, requirement or decision of said city council, any time may take an appeal to the superior court of the county. Said appeal to the superior court shall be the same as an appeal to the superior court from any decision made by the court, except, however, that said appeal may be filed within 30 days from the date of the decision of the city council or of any official charged with the enforcement of any order, requirement or decision in connection therewith; and upon failure to file said appeal within 30 days, the said decision of the city council shall be final.
(Ord. of 8-11-1998, § 13-10)
